stitch_shortlist.author: clemfom
stitch_shortlist.claim: Put a pimple patch on ANY wound to ‘draw out moisture’

pitch.the_claim: You can slap a hydrocolloid pimple patch on ANY wound and it’ll ‘draw out’ moisture — not just a pimple.
pitch.why_it_stitches: 6.8M views in 3.3d, 2.4K comments; confidently backwards on how hydrocolloid works and risky on open or deep wounds.
pitch.your_fit: You’ve said derms get pimples too and use hydrocolloid patches (with salicylic acid / tea tree) to clear a whitehead faster. NEW angle: patches ABSORB fluid from a shallow, closed pimple — they don’t detox or ‘draw out’ anything from a deep or open wound, which needs real wound care.
angles: ‘You want me to WHAT?’: a patch on an open wound
Empathy-first: here’s what hydrocolloid actually does
Switch-don’t-quit: when a patch helps vs when to get it looked at

stitch_shortlist.author: saleslionglass
stitch_shortlist.claim: Skin-cancer rose WITH sunscreen sales → ‘sunscreen causes cancer’

pitch.the_claim: ‘Skin-cancer rates climbed for decades while sunscreen sales skyrocketed— so oxybenzone/octinoxate sunscreens must cause it.’
pitch.why_it_stitches: Classic correlation-≠-causation misinformation and exactly the viral sunscreen myth derms are fighting this summer (homemade beef-tallow ‘sunscreen,’ etc.). 459K and spreading — not huge (rubric miss), but dangerous.
pitch.your_fit: You teach that US sunscreens are heavily FDA-restricted and that daily broad-spectrum SPF is the least-glamorous, most-effective anti-aging and anti-cancer step there is. Correct the correlation trap without shaming.
angles: Myth-bust: more diagnoses ≠ sunscreen causing them
Reassure: oxybenzone safety data — and mineral options if worried
Switch-don’t-quit: pick a sunscreen you’ll actually wear
